item.title: Privacy Reform – Consultation on Exposure Draft legislation

proposed_record.title: Draft bill to strengthen the Privacy Act 1988
proposed_record.summary: The Australian Government has released the Exposure Draft Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026 to modernise and strengthen privacy law. The Bill is a draft and the government is still considering it.
what_changes: The draft Bill proposes amendments to the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the economy-wide framework for handling personal information.
The reforms aim to address risks from new technologies, including AI and wearable devices such as smart glasses.
The government says the Bill aims to give regulated entities greater certainty.
proposed_record.who_it_applies_to: Law practices that are regulated entities under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

history.event: Exposure Draft Bill and Consultation Paper released for consultation, which closed on 18 September 2026.
